Netflix has become one of the most ideologically consistent streaming platforms in Hollywood. Its 2024 library ranges from outright progressive propaganda to legitimately entertaining action films that avoid the lecture circuit. We ran every Netflix title in the VirtueVigil database through our Woke-Watch Scoring System and ranked them from most woke to most traditional. If you want to know where to start -- or what to skip -- this list is your guide.

Rankings run from highest woke score to most traditional. Scores measure the density and consistency of progressive ideological content relative to runtime. They are not quality ratings. A high woke score means the film pushes an agenda. A high trad score means it reinforces traditional values. Both can produce great or terrible entertainment.

#1 - Emilia Perez (2024) — STRONGLY WOKE

Woke Score: 28.0 • Score Margin: -22 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

Jacques Audiard's French-language film about a Mexican cartel boss who transitions to a woman collected 13 Oscar nominations -- the most ever for a non-English-language film. The premise is the politics: the cartel life is framed as a masculine prison, with the transition coded as moral rebirth and liberation. Netflix acquired it after a Cannes sweep and pushed it hard through awards season. The film is visually inventive and genuinely strange, but the ideological framework is inseparable from the story. Every scene reinforces the same thesis. The Academy loved it. Most audiences who actually watched it did not.

#2 - Adolescence (2025) — WOKE LEAN

Woke Score: 22.54 • Score Margin: -8 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

This four-episode Netflix miniseries about a 13-year-old boy arrested for murder became one of the most watched Netflix originals of 2025. Each episode is shot in a single continuous take. The craft is extraordinary. The ideology is consistent: the story uses online radicalization and misogyny as the lens for every character decision, from the parents to the police to the boy himself. Netflix positioned it as prestige television, and by technical standards it qualifies. The progressive framework around male violence and digital radicalization is woven into every conversation and every silence. It lands at -8 WOKE not because it hides its agenda, but because the filmmaking never lets that agenda become a substitute for character.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Adolescence

#3 - KPop Demon Hunters (2025) — WOKE LEAN

Woke Score: 24.18 • Score Margin: -8 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

Sony and Netflix's animated musical sends three K-pop idol women to battle a patriarchal demon king whose boy band minions are literally demons. Co-director Maggie Kang confirmed that lead character Rumi's identity arc is an explicit coming-out allegory. The queer themes are front-loaded and never disguised. The animation is gorgeous, the music is genuinely good, and the film earned two Oscar nominations. Conservative audiences can make an informed decision within the first ten minutes. It scored -8 WOKE because the progressive content is visible and consistent, not because it ambushes you. Knowing that going in changes the experience significantly.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of KPop Demon Hunters

#4 - Bridgerton Season 4 (2026) — WOKE LEAN

Woke Score: 16.2 • Score Margin: -6 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

Shonda Rhimes's Regency romance franchise returns with Benedict Bridgerton's story and a Cinderella structure that works romantically but can't decide whether it wants to be fantasy escapism or class commentary. Benedict's bisexuality is introduced and largely left on the table. The casting continues the show's race-blind approach to Regency England. The romance mechanics are effective. The political undertow is constant: every relationship carries an implicit critique of aristocratic hierarchy. It scores -6 WOKE because the progressive framework is embedded in the genre rather than announced, which makes it more insidious and more watchable than most agenda-first television.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Bridgerton Season 4

#5 - Stranger Things Season 5 (2025) — WOKE LEAN

Woke Score: 13.0 • Score Margin: -5 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

The Duffer Brothers wrapped their 80s nostalgia horror epic with a final season that critics praised and audiences watched in record numbers. The show's progressive elements have grown season by season: queer representation, diverse casting, and occasional messaging about outcasts versus mainstream culture. The horror mechanics remain the strength. The ideology is secondary and never dominates the storytelling, which is why it lands at -5 rather than lower. Long-time fans of the show who have watched since Season 1 will find the final season consistent with what came before. Conservative viewers who enjoyed the earlier seasons will find it unchanged in tenor.

#6 - The Electric State (2025) — WOKE LEAN

Woke Score: 13.63 • Score Margin: -4 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

The Russo Brothers adapted Simon Stalenhag's illustrated novel into a $320 million production that earned tepid reviews and middling audience scores. Millie Bobby Brown searches for her missing brother in a retro-futuristic America ruled by corporations and drone warfare. The critique of corporate power and military technology is embedded throughout. Chris Pratt provides most of the entertainment value. The film's progressive framework around government overreach and corporate violence is genuine, but the spectacle is the priority. It lands at -4 WOKE because the messaging is consistent but secondary to the action-adventure mechanics. A mediocre film ideologically consistent with Netflix's brand positioning.

#7 - Ozark (2022) — WOKE LEAN

Woke Score: 9.0 • Score Margin: -4 WOKE • Platform: Netflix

Netflix's crime drama ran four seasons and concluded with a finale that divided fans. The Byrde family's descent into cartel money laundering maintains a cynical view of American institutions throughout: law enforcement is corrupt, religion is weaponized, and the professional class uses the system to avoid consequences. Marty and Wendy Byrde are compelling precisely because they are morally hollow. The show does not moralize -- it observes with clinical detachment. The -4 WOKE score reflects the show's consistently progressive institutional critique rather than identity politics content. The final season ends with a statement about consequences that some found satisfying and others found evasive.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Ozark

#8 - Rebel Ridge (2024) — TRADITIONAL

Woke Score: 8.18 • Score Margin: +10 TRAD • Platform: Netflix

Jeremy Saulnier's Netflix original about a former Marine cyclist who goes up against a corrupt small-town police department is one of the best action films Netflix has produced. Aaron Pierre is magnetic. The action is precise and brutal. The film's critique of police corruption and civil asset forfeiture is pointed, but it lands on the traditional side of the ledger because it centers individual competence, moral clarity, and physical courage against institutional corruption. The hero wins through superior skill and determination. The film does not ask viewers to feel guilty -- it asks them to root for the underdog with overwhelming capability. +10 TRAD because righteous individual wins cleanly.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Rebel Ridge

#9 - Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F (2024) — TRADITIONAL

Woke Score: 4.0 • Score Margin: +11 TRAD • Platform: Netflix

Eddie Murphy returned to one of his signature roles after three decades and delivered exactly what audiences wanted: Axel Foley running his mouth at full speed in Beverly Hills, solving a conspiracy that threatens his estranged daughter. No ideology. No messaging. Pure entertainment from a star doing what made him famous. The original cast returns. The chemistry holds. Netflix paid for a legacy sequel and got one that works on every level it was designed to work on. +11 TRAD because it celebrates a father protecting his daughter through competence, humor, and refusing to follow rules.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F

#10 - Nonnas (2025) — TRADITIONAL

Woke Score: 1.0 • Score Margin: +16 TRAD • Platform: Netflix

Based on the true story of Jody Scaravella, who hired Italian grandmothers to cook at his Staten Island restaurant after his mother died, this Netflix film is a rare thing: a movie about family, food, grief, and community that has no interest in ideology whatsoever. The nonnas are real people. The food is real. The story is about a man honoring his mother's memory by building something that keeps her world alive. Adam Sandler produces. The film is warm, specific, and genuinely moving. +16 TRAD because it takes family, tradition, and the passing of culture between generations completely seriously.

This ranking covers every Netflix title currently reviewed in the VirtueVigil database. The full picture is complicated: Netflix produces both the most woke prestige content and some genuinely entertaining traditional fare. The pattern is that original dramatic series and prestige films lean progressive, while action films and legacy sequels tend to avoid ideology. Plan your Netflix queue accordingly -- and browse the full VirtueVigil review database at virtuevigil.com/reviews/ for detailed trope-by-trope breakdowns on every title.
